title: Why Antibiotics Are a Shared Resource
title_ja: 抗菌薬が社会全体の資源といえる理由
fact_notes: 背景となる考え方は添付の資料で確認。本文と練習問題は新規制作。例示した人物・学校・活動は架空の説明用設定。

sentences.en: A student recovering from an illness hears that antibiotics have helped many people survive bacterial infections that were once difficult to treat.
sentences.ja: 病気から回復中の生徒は、抗菌薬がかつて治療困難だった細菌感染症から多くの人を救ったと聞きます。

sentences.en: The student wonders why health organizations warn against using these important medicines when they are not needed.
sentences.ja: 生徒はなぜ保健機関が重要な薬を不要なときに使わないよう警告するのか疑問に思います。

sentences.en: However, the concern is not that antibiotics are generally harmful when used appropriately under professional guidance.
sentences.ja: しかし懸念は専門家の指導のもとで適切に使う抗菌薬が一般的に有害だということではありません。

sentences.en: It is that microorganisms can develop resistance, making certain medicines less effective against the infections they were designed to treat.
sentences.ja: 微生物が耐性を持ち、薬が対象とする感染症への効果が低下する場合があるという問題です。

sentences.en: The World Health Organization identifies antimicrobial resistance as a serious threat to health systems around the world.
sentences.ja: 世界保健機関は薬剤耐性を世界の医療制度に対する重大な脅威としています。

sentences.en: The challenge shows how a decision about treatment can have implications for people beyond the individual receiving the medicine.
sentences.ja: この課題は治療の判断が薬を受け取る本人以外にも影響し得ることを示します。

sentences.en: Understanding that shared responsibility begins with distinguishing the appropriate use of a medicine from its unnecessary use.
sentences.ja: その共有責任を理解するには薬の適切な使用と不必要な使用を区別することから始まります。

sentences.en: Antibiotics are designed to treat certain bacterial infections, but they do not work against viruses that cause many common illnesses.
sentences.ja: 抗菌薬は特定の細菌感染症を治療するためのもので、多くの一般的な病気の原因となるウイルスには効きません。

sentences.en: For example, taking an antibiotic for a viral infection will not make that virus disappear simply because the medicine helped with a different illness.
sentences.ja: 例えば別の病気に効いたからといってウイルス感染症で抗菌薬を飲んでもそのウイルスは消えません。

sentences.en: Using medicines unnecessarily can contribute to the wider problem of resistance by creating conditions that favor resistant microorganisms.
sentences.ja: 薬を不必要に使うと耐性微生物に有利な条件を作り、耐性という広い問題に寄与する可能性があります。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, patients should not decide on their own to avoid or stop prescribed treatment because they have heard about resistance.
sentences.ja: それでも耐性の話を聞いたからといって患者が自分で処方された治療を避けたり中止したりすべきではありません。

sentences.en: Decisions about whether an antibiotic is needed and how it should be taken require qualified clinical judgment.
sentences.ja: 抗菌薬が必要か、どう服用すべきかは資格ある医療専門家の判断が必要です。

sentences.en: Responsible information explains the risk without encouraging people to ignore professional medical advice.
sentences.ja: 責任ある情報は専門的な医療助言を無視するよう促さずに危険を説明します。

sentences.en: Resistance is shaped by more than the actions of patients in a single country or hospital.
sentences.ja: 耐性は一国や一病院の患者の行動だけで決まるものではありません。

sentences.en: In addition, access to clean water, infection prevention, diagnostic testing, and appropriate treatment can influence how infections spread and are managed.
sentences.ja: さらに清潔な水、感染予防、検査、適切な治療へのアクセスは感染の拡大と管理に影響します。

sentences.en: A clinic with limited testing resources may face difficult decisions that cannot be explained by blaming individual patients.
sentences.ja: 検査資源が限られた診療所は個々の患者を責めるだけでは説明できない難しい判断に直面するかもしれません。

sentences.en: Health professionals also need reliable information about which medicines remain effective against particular infections.
sentences.ja: 医療専門家には特定の感染症に対しどの薬がまだ有効かという信頼できる情報も必要です。

sentences.en: International monitoring helps public health institutions identify patterns, although no single number describes every region equally well.
sentences.ja: 国際的な監視は公衆衛生機関がパターンを特定するのに役立ちますが、一つの数字で全地域を同じように説明できるわけではありません。

sentences.en: The WHO emphasizes surveillance and coordinated action rather than treating antimicrobial resistance as a problem with one simple solution.
sentences.ja: WHOは薬剤耐性を一つの単純な解決策で済む問題とせず、監視と協調した行動を重視します。

sentences.en: Public policy must consider both protecting medicines' effectiveness and ensuring that people who need treatment can receive it.
sentences.ja: 公共政策は薬の有効性を守ることと必要な人が治療を受けられることの両方を考える必要があります。

sentences.en: A school health club decides to prepare a public information poster about antibiotics and responsibility.
sentences.ja: 学校の保健部は抗菌薬と責任についての情報ポスターを作ることにします。

sentences.en: Some members propose a slogan saying that nobody should use antibiotics because resistance is dangerous.
sentences.ja: 耐性が危険だから誰も抗菌薬を使うべきでないという標語を提案する部員もいます。

sentences.en: However, classmates point out that such an absolute message would misrepresent the medical benefits of appropriate treatment.
sentences.ja: しかしクラスメートはその絶対的な表現が適切な治療の利益を誤って伝えると指摘します。

sentences.en: The students instead explain that antibiotics should be used when clinically appropriate and according to qualified medical advice.
sentences.ja: 生徒は代わりに医学的に適切なとき専門家の助言に従って抗菌薬を使用すべきと説明します。

sentences.en: They include a reminder that public health challenges involve hospitals, governments, researchers, and communities as well as individual patients.
sentences.ja: また公衆衛生の課題には患者個人だけでなく病院、政府、研究者、地域社会が関わると示します。

sentences.en: Their final poster avoids promising a perfect solution and encourages readers to seek trustworthy medical information.
sentences.ja: 最終ポスターは完璧な解決を約束せず、信頼できる医療情報を求めるよう促します。

sentences.en: The lesson is that protecting a shared medical resource requires both careful personal decisions and effective health systems.
sentences.ja: 共有の医療資源を守るには個人の慎重な判断と有効な医療制度の両方が必要だという学びです。

options: Preserving antibiotic effectiveness requires appropriate medical use and coordinated public health measures.
Every infection is caused by bacteria.
Resistance is only a problem for individual patients.
questions.explanation_ja: 適切な使用と社会的な対策の両立が主題です。

questions.prompt: Which infections are antibiotics intended to treat?
questions.explanation_ja: 特定の細菌感染症です。

questions.prompt: Why is it misleading to say no one should take antibiotics?
options: Properly prescribed antibiotics can provide important medical benefits.
questions.explanation_ja: 適切な治療の有効性を無視するからです。

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about viral illnesses?
options: They are always treated by antibiotics.
Every virus develops in the same way.
Antibiotics do not directly work against the viruses causing them.
questions.explanation_ja: ウイルスには効かないと説明します。

questions.prompt: Why might clinics with limited testing face special challenges?
options: They may need to make decisions without enough diagnostic information.
Every infection requires the same medicine.
questions.explanation_ja: 検査情報が不足することがあるためです。

questions.prompt: What does international monitoring help institutions do?
options: Identify broad patterns of antimicrobial resistance.
Guarantee a cure for every infection.
questions.explanation_ja: 耐性の傾向を捉える助けになります。

options: Systematic observation and monitoring of health information.
questions.explanation_ja: surveillanceは継続的な監視・調査です。

questions.prompt: What slogan do some students initially suggest?
options: Take medicines whenever you feel tired.
All patients should choose their own treatment.
Nobody should use antibiotics because resistance is dangerous.
questions.explanation_ja: すべての抗菌薬使用を否定する標語です。

questions.prompt: Why does the final poster mention hospitals and governments?
options: Resistance requires coordinated action beyond individual choices.
Every country has the same health system.
questions.explanation_ja: 問題が個人だけでなく制度にも関わるためです。

questions.prompt: What is the role of the final sentence?
options: To emphasize personal decisions and functioning health systems as shared responsibilities.
To claim only researchers can act.
questions.explanation_ja: 個人と制度の双方の責任が結論です。
